newsitem.title: BURMA: World War Two veterans reconcile in Burma.
newsitem.headline: World War Two veterans reconcile in Burma.

text.p: Japanese and British World War Two veterans who fought against each other more than half a century ago met and reconciled on Saturday at an emotional ceremony held for the first time in their former battleground of Burma.
"We fought to death in very savage battles here," Philip Malins, a former British army soldier, told Reuters at the ceremony.
"We are glad that they (our enemies) are still alive now. We believe in reconciliation. It is desperately important," he said with tears welling up in his eyes.
"Victory without reconciliation is never complete because bitterness goes on if there is no reconciliation."

The ceremony held at a Japanese cemetery in central Rangoon was attended by nine members of the Britain-based "Burma Campaign Fellowship Group" and 36 members of the Japan-based "All Burma Veteran Association of Japan".
The two groups have held reconciliation ceremonies many times before, but this was their first on Burmese soil.
More than 190,000 Japanese soldiers and 37,000 allied soldiers mainly from Britain, Australia, New Zealand and India died in the battles in Burma during the World War Two.
